class.name: RenderQualitySettings
class.brief_description: Settings resource of [RenderQualitySettingsServer]: 3D scaling, mesh LOD, anti-aliasing, variable rate shading and occlusion culling.
class.description: The data of the settings domain [code]"render_quality"[/code]. [RenderQualitySettingsServer] keeps three copies of it (defaults, applied and pending values, see [method SettingsServer.get_settings]) and stores it in [code]user://settings/render_quality.ini[/code]. Change the values through the methods of [RenderQualitySettingsServer] or [method SettingsServer.set_value], not on the resource, so that they are validated and applied. The setters store values as they are; [RenderQualitySettingsServer] clamps values out of range and replaces invalid enum values with the default, with a warning, when they are set or loaded. Values the current renderer ignores are stored too, so that the same file works with every renderer. It can also be used as the project defaults of the domain: save a [RenderQualitySettings] as a [code].tres[/code] file and name it in the project setting [code]settings/defaults/render_quality[/code].

members.member: The sharpening of FSR 1.0 and FSR 2.2, pushed to [member Viewport.fsr_sharpness]. [code]0.0[/code] is the sharpest, [code]2.0[/code] the softest. Valid range: [code]0.0[/code] to [code]2.0[/code]. Forward+ only: not supported in the Mobile and Compatibility renderers.

The automatic mesh LOD threshold in pixels, pushed to [member Viewport.mesh_lod_threshold]. Higher values use simpler meshes sooner (faster, more visible pop-in). Valid range: [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1024.0[/code]. Works in every renderer.
The multisample anti-aliasing of 2D (canvas items), pushed to [member Viewport.msaa_2d]. Works in every renderer, including the Compatibility renderer and the Web export.

The multisample anti-aliasing of 3D, pushed to [member Viewport.msaa_3d]. Works in every renderer, including the Compatibility renderer and the Web export (WebGL 2). MetalFX Temporal scaling turns it off internally.

The quality of the occlusion culling BVH, pushed to [method RenderingServer.viewport_set_occlusion_culling_build_quality] (global, for all viewports). Lower quality builds faster when occluders move. Not supported without the [code]raycast[/code] module.

The number of occlusion rays per thread, pushed to [method RenderingServer.viewport_set_occlusion_rays_per_thread] (global, for all viewports). Fewer rays are faster on the CPU, but may cull objects that should be visible. Valid range: [code]1[/code] to [code]2048[/code]. Not supported without the [code]raycast[/code] module.

The 3D scaling mode, pushed to [member Viewport.scaling_3d_mode]. Bilinear and Nearest work in every renderer; FSR 1.0 and FSR 2.2 need the Forward+ renderer; MetalFX needs Metal (macOS, iOS), MetalFX Temporal also the Forward+ renderer. A mode the current renderer can't use is stored, but bilinear scaling is used (see [method RenderQualitySettingsServer.is_scaling_3d_mode_supported]).

The 3D render scale, pushed to [member Viewport.scaling_3d_scale]. Below [code]1.0[/code] renders 3D at a lower resolution (faster), above [code]1.0[/code] supersamples. Valid range: [code]0.1[/code] to [code]2.0[/code]. Works in every renderer.
The screen-space anti-aliasing (FXAA or SMAA), pushed to [member Viewport.screen_space_aa]. Not supported in the Compatibility renderer.
If [code]true[/code], debanding is used, pushed to [member Viewport.use_debanding]. Not supported in the Compatibility renderer.

If [code]true[/code], occlusion culling is used, pushed to [member Viewport.use_occlusion_culling]. It can be switched at any time, but only has an effect if the scene has baked [OccluderInstance3D] nodes; enable [member ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/use_occlusion_culling] in the project so that the editor bakes them. Runs on the CPU in every renderer; not supported without the [code]raycast[/code] module.
If [code]true[/code], temporal anti-aliasing is used, pushed to [member Viewport.use_taa]. Forward+ only: not supported in the Mobile and Compatibility renderers.

The variable rate shading mode, pushed to [member Viewport.vrs_mode]. [constant Viewport.VRS_TEXTURE] uses [member Viewport.vrs_texture] (the root viewport gets it from [member ProjectSettings.rendering/vrs/texture]), [constant Viewport.VRS_XR] the XR interface. Needs a GPU with variable rate shading in the Forward+ or Mobile renderer; not supported in the Compatibility renderer.
